newsitem.title: USA: USDA seeks input on Australia meat inspection plan.
newsitem.headline: USDA seeks input on Australia meat inspection plan.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department said Friday it is seeking comment on a proposed pilot program in Australia that would replace government meat inspectors with plant employees.
In a notice published in the Federal Register, the USDA said Australia's proposed program would focus on inspection for pathogenic microorganisms and chemical residues.

The agency's Food Safety and Inspection Service arm said it wanted public comment on whether the inspection program detailed in the Australian proposal would ensure equivalence and the safety, wholesomeness, and truthful labeling of product produced under such a system.
The Australian government asked that meat from the plants participating in the pilot program maintain access to export markets, including the United States, the USDA said.
Written comments must be submitted to the agency by July 29.

As a result of the World Trade Organization (WTO) agreement on sanitary and phytosanitary measures, the United States and other nations agreed to harmonize their animal and plant health import requirements.
